name: Warehouse — First Delivery
narrative: The practice warehouse has one waiting order and one outbound station. The robot already knows the fixed aisle route, but it does not understand warehouse work yet: it will walk over a package and pass the delivery station unless you give it interaction rules. Teach it that a package under its wheels should be picked up, and that a carried package at a delivery station should be unloaded. The world is not complete when the robot reaches a square; it is complete when the order is delivered.
objective: Pick up the waiting package and deliver it to Outbound A.
learningObjective: World interaction: use observations about packages and delivery zones to choose the engine-owned Pick Up and Deliver actions.
intelligenceExplanation: The route rules are already in place, so the robot can travel through every aisle. What is missing are the two moments of work: when a package is here, pick it up; when at a delivery zone while carrying a package, deliver it. Make both rules higher priority than continuing along the aisle. Unlike a maze, this world completes immediately after the final successful delivery — no goal holding is needed.
hint: Add WHEN packageHere → DO pick-up with high priority. Then add WHEN deliveryHere AND carryingPackage → DO deliver with an even higher priority.
hints: The route is present already. Watch the debug panel for Package here and Delivery here.
A package needs an interaction rule, not another move rule: WHEN packageHere → DO pick-up.
Delivery must only happen while carrying cargo: WHEN deliveryHere AND carryingPackage → DO deliver. Give both interaction rules higher priority than 60.
brief: Teach the robot to pick up the waiting order and drop it at Outbound A.
context: One order, one outbound dock. The robot already drives the aisle — it just doesn't do warehouse work yet.
